text:
With Nathan MacKinnon out about 12 weeks, as the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal reported, Colorado's center depth chart now starts with Brock Nelson, and his minutes show it: 21.5, 18.7 and 19.7 in the last three games, up from around 16 earlier in the month. He answered with three points against Anaheim and two assists against Montreal.

At 35 and past 1,000 career games, Nelson has 18 points in 24 games, eight on the power play. The finishing is a bit hot (eight goals on 6.2 expected, an 18% shooting rate), and the Avalanche are getting lucky with him on the ice too. But the underlying play is good: they take about 58% of expected goals at five on five with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile of forwards for driving play last season, though with very strong linemates.

That last part is the question now. Much of what made his numbers look so clean came with elite teammates. What to watch is how his chances hold up against top matchups without MacKinnon.
headline: Nelson's turn at the top of the lineup
